      <title>UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/26/uk-sanctions-sudanese-military-leaders-implicated-in-el-fasher-campaign-of</link>
      <description><p>Commanders suspected of sexual violence during the largest and fastest slaughter of civilians in more than 30 years have been subjected to travel ban and asset freeze</p><p>Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/mar/25/heroism-horror-and-the-pits-of-hell-inside-the-last-days-of-el-fasher">mass atrocity</a> that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.</p><p>A year after the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2025/nov/02/he-told-the-world-what-was-happening-in-el-fasher-then-they-sought-him-out-how-sudan-lost-a-true-hero-of-the-war">fall of El Fasher</a>, the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/26/uk-sanctions-sudanese-military-leaders-implicated-in-el-fasher-campaign-of">Continue reading...</a></description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e2ce5e36-d1cc-11f1-a1b1-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/a76378f2ae9959050b5482d797377dd5c2291e0f.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e2ce5e36-d1cc-11f1-a1b1-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/a76378f2ae9959050b5482d797377dd5c2291e0f.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">45cc8ee8-d25b-11f1-9fd9-273a6902d26e</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 23:14:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e2ce5e36-d1cc-11f1-a1b1-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/a76378f2ae9959050b5482d797377dd5c2291e0f.jpg">© Aaron Chown, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Israel election: Record turnout as Netanyahu and Eisenkot remain deadlocked</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261027-israel-election-record-turnout-netanyahu-eisenkot-deadlock</link><description>
Israel's election remained deadlocked on Tuesday, exit polls showed, with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's bloc narrowly ahead of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp by 52 seats to 50. Neither side had a clear path to forming a government. Voter turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e0844dc0-d24e-11f1-bac3-bf69a9ce9852/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-27T201655Z-2088081210-RC2WBOANCXWD-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-ELECTION.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e0844dc0-d24e-11f1-bac3-bf69a9ce9852/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-27T201655Z-2088081210-RC2WBOANCXWD-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-ELECTION.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">df034636-d258-11f1-b9bc-e9013cf76742</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 22:58:53 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e0844dc0-d24e-11f1-bac3-bf69a9ce9852/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-27T201655Z-2088081210-RC2WBOANCXWD-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-ELECTION.jpg">© Shir Torem, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Israel: First exit polls show no clear winner, Arab parties make gains</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261027-israel-first-exit-polls-show-no-clear-winner-arab-parties-make-gains</link><description>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Tue, 27 Oct 2026 21:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space ]]> I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater.

On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My "spacesuit" was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks, or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments. Being underwater, if we encountered a major problem with our gear, we would have had to treat it as seriously as if we were astronauts on the International Space Station. There was no immediate "out." This was serious.

Before this underwater mission, I had worked as the commander of nearly 40 analog missions that simulated crewed missions to the moon and Mars. The goal of these types of missions is to test what living and working in lunar or Martian environments might be like. We study everything from the psychology of living in extreme conditions, or in isolation, to the technology that astronauts might use to complete those missions successfully.

Testing spacesuit technology is also an important part of these analog space missions. These suits are usually a much simpler version of the ones astronauts use in space, which can weigh around 310 pounds (141 kilograms) when fully equipped with life support systems.

Analog spacesuits usually weigh a maximum of 30 pounds (14 kg). While there are many differences between suits designed for use in space and these suits designed for testing on Earth, the biggest one is that, on an analog mission, crew members can open their helmets and breathe the outside air if necessary.

Astronauts in space don’t have that advantage. But neither do aquanauts, those performing a simulated space mission underwater.

Aquanauts spend at least 24 hours underwater in a so-called state of saturation. That’s a physiological condition achieved by a person who breathes underwater long enough for the body’s tissues to absorb the maximum possible amount of inert gas (like nitrogen), for a specific depth and pressure.

Water leaking into our suits or into our underwater habitat can pose serious risks for the crew, as well as health problems related to the higher pressures underwater, amongst other challenges unique to this environment.

This is what pushed me to be extra thorough, and perhaps even a bit paranoid, when preparing for my scuba diving "spacewalks." While scuba diving, the dangers of your equipment failing or decompression sickness can be as lethal as some of the difficulties astronauts face during their spacewalks. That’s why we follow strict protocols when preparing to go on underwater EVAs and during the outings themselves.

As an experienced scuba diver, I wasn’t concerned with the scuba diving aspect of the mission itself. In many ways, it was much easier than some dives in pitch black water I performed in the open ocean or cave dives. But for these EVAs, I was more on edge because I was the Commander of the SEA STAR crew living 22 feet (7 meters) underwater in the station, called the Jules’ Undersea Lab, in Florida. Being responsible for other people’s lives made me extra cautious and also more worried than usual when diving.

Despite the many challenges of these underwater EVAs, these experiences and lessons learned can teach us a lot about what we still need to improve for future long-duration space missions.

Our aquanaut "spacesuits" were essentially the same as scuba gear, with the exception of two important accessories that aren’t always necessary for normal dives. Those were gloves and flashlights. We needed the gloves as protection from a number of factors in the environment around us, like barnacles and other sharp natural formations. They also made using cameras and vacuums for environmental cleaning underwater more challenging, which was a good approximation for how gloves limit astronauts’ dexterity during spacewalks.

The underwater environment around us had very low visibility, which is why the flashlights were a mandatory component of our EVAs. They helped us to navigate through the darkness and find each other. Even still, with just the small flash of light we could only see a couple of feet ahead of us. That is why it was also vital that we worked together and moved side-by-side.

Good communication skills were another crucial component of our underwater simulated space mission. Before each EVA, we prepared a plan, talked about backup plans and went over emergency procedures. During the EVA, we used standard scuba diving sign language to communicate, and we created some new mission-specific signals as well. This visual communication is very useful during simulated space missions on land, too, especially in situations when our communications technologies have not worked properly.

No matter how much we prepared, though, the fear of the unknown and of getting lost can still get to a crew. A common safety protocol when diving is to safely return to the surface if you get lost or separated from your team and cannot find them. However, during the SEA STAR mission, we planned on staying underwater for the full five-day duration of our mission. That meant that such an option was out of the question, except of course in emergency scenarios.

Personally, I enjoyed the challenge of the low visibility in new terrain. It allowed me to hone my orientation and navigation skills, as well as my abilities as a leader in challenging environments. Though I was more vigilant than I perhaps needed to be, once I dove out of our submerged station, I went straight into my favorite mode: exploration. Despite not being able to see very much ahead of me, and all while keeping a watchful eye on my crewmembers, I finally truly felt like an astronaut on a spacewalk. Darkness was all around me, but my determination and curiosity propelled me toward exploring the unknown.

]]> <![CDATA[ Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart ]]> Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago.

That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way. What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart.

Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf. But on rare occasions, the supernova doesn't completely destroy the star, and a shattered stellar body remains, called a zombie star. These events are called Type Iax supernovas.

Pa 30 was first identified in 2013 by a citizen scientist in 2013, but scientists soon linked it to a cosmic explosion recorded independently in the year 1181 in Japanese, Chinese, and Arabic historical documentation. That makes this one of only five supernovas seen before the invention of the telescope.

"Reliable historical records of stellar explosions extend back only about a thousand years. For all we know, there might well be similar remnants still lurking in the dark in our own galaxy," team member Ilaria Caiazzo, assistant professor at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA), said in a statement.

"Today, we are lucky to study an intriguing object we know was observed by astronomers who made three independent historical records of the event centuries before the invention of the telescope."

Solar system-sized pearls

Pa 30 is a good laboratory to study supernovas because, at around 7,500 light-years away, it is relatively close to Earth on cosmic scales. For instance, the heart of our galaxy is around 26,000 light-years away. "We can see this much detail because of Pa 30's proximity to Earth," said Caiazzo. "This proximity makes Pa 30 uniquely valuable for study."

It is also an important subject of study because it is the only supernova remnant in which we can see a zombie star.

Using the Gemini North telescope, Caiazzo and colleagues zoomed in on Pa 30, discovering knots along the strands of gas radiating out from the site of the cosmic explosion, like pearls on a string.

These pearls are each wide enough to encompass the orbit of Neptune, the most distant planet from the sun, ten times over.

"The planetary region of our solar system could fit in each knot about ten times with room to spare," said Caiazzo. "The knots are quite strikingly uniform. We are excited to try to model them."

The team also discovered that the zombie star sits almost perfectly at the heart of Pa 30. When these cosmic explosions happen, they should provide any debris, including zombie stars, with a kick. The fact that this "living dead" star still sits dead center of this wreckage suggests that when this explosion happened, it was roughly symmetrical and the kick was relatively light.

"Explosions conserve momentum. If the explosion itself was perfectly symmetric, the ejecta should also be symmetric, and the surviving star should not receive a substantial kick," Caiazzo said. "We were able to measure a precise upper limit of the remnant star's transverse kick speed, showing that it was surprisingly small. We practically don't see the star moving away at all."

While there are still many mysteries surrounding Pa 30 and its zombie occupant, one of the most exciting prospects emerging from this research is the possibility it will help identify the wreckage of other Type Iax supernovas in our galaxy.

"While we can see Type Iax supernovas in distant galaxies as point sources of light, resolving the remnants of such explosions is only possible in our own galaxy and in very few nearby ones," Caiazzo concluded. "Eventually, we plan to use Pa 30's distinctive properties to search the Milky Way and nearby galaxies for similar objects."

Koenig is survived by his sole daughter, screenwriter and actress Danielle Koenig.

Their baffling nature has prompted a range of potential explanations, most of which focus on a variety of unexplained natural phenomena occurring in Earth's atmosphere. However, a few more far-out possibilities, including potential evidence of extraterrestrial technology, have also been considered.

What do we know?

A curious discovery

The enigma of long-delayed echoes has perplexed scientists since their initial detection by Hals, who at the time reported his odd findings to Norwegian physicist Carl Størmer. This prompted an investigation by Størmer with physicist Balthasar van der Pol, during which the duo was able to reproduce the phenomenon but were unsuccessful in determining its cause.

Since those early observations, ongoing reports of long-delayed echoes have continued to be recorded. Under normal conditions, radio echoes occur whenever a radio signal reflects or "bounces" off an object, although other conditions such as signals traveling through a delayed path can also cause echoes to occur.

Long delayed echoes, by contrast, are generally characterized by radio signals that return after more than 2.7 seconds following their original transmission, although the terminology has sometimes been applied more broadly.

Complicating investigations into this unusual brand of radio phenomena over the years has been their unpredictable nature, along with significant reported variances in the timing and nature of the delays, which has made it difficult for researchers to narrow down a single cause.

Possible explanations

Despite the challenges presented by this unique class of space mysteries, there are several theories that have been put forward over the years about what could cause long-delayed echoes.

In the mid 1980s, researchers R. J. Vidmar and F. W. Crawford conducted experiments in Alaska that aimed to detect long-delayed echoes, which built on earlier research they published involving possible detections in 1970. According to their findings at the time, Vidmar and Crawford hypothesized that radio signals could be captured between ionized layers in the atmosphere and "guided" over long distances.

More recently, University of Oslo researcher Sverre Holm has advanced a similar concept that he calls magnetospherically ducted echo (MDE), in which radio waves may become trapped within electrically charged regions of Earth's upper atmosphere and guided along magnetic field lines extending far into the magnetosphere. Under certain conditions, these signals may reach as far away as the opposite hemisphere before they are "bounced" back toward Earth, resulting in the delayed echo effect.

According to Holm, MDE "is the best understood mechanism for long delayed echoes" out of five promising explanations he outlines, adding that based on the MDE model, such long delayed echoes "can be predicted to what seems like about 5 ms accuracy using a simple model for the magnetic field lines."

Still, one problem that arises involves the relatively short delays associated with this mechanism, which may not necessarily account for the much longer, multi-second echoes reported in some historical observations. Since radio waves travel at close to the speed of light, a signal could theoretically cover distances equivalent to the planet's circumference several times in a single second. First, the historical echoes were detected at approximately 9.55 MHz, well above the 1–4 MHz frequency range typically associated with MDEs. Additionally, historical LDEs reportedly exhibited delays ranging from 3 to 30 seconds, whereas MDEs generally produce delays of only a few hundred milliseconds.

Finally, a similar line of investigation has looked at whether clouds of plasma originating from the sun might also be able to produce the well-characterized echo effect.

What remains unknown?

Extraterrestrial origins?

Although scientific research has identified several promising explanations for long-delayed echoes, the mysterious nature of these events has also inspired more speculative theories over the decades, including some involving the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

Lunan's theory essentially went like this: an extraterrestrial civilization in the Epsilon Boötis system had deployed a hypothetical autonomous communications probe (known as a Bracewell probe) to Earth in the distant past, which had been comfortably orbiting in one of Earth's gravitationally stable Lagrange points for thousands of years.

While few modern researchers seriously consider extraterrestrial hypotheses to explain long-delayed echoes, these obscure phenomena remain intriguing, even as ongoing research sheds light on their possible causes. Explanations such as Sverre Holm's magnetospherically ducted echo model offer promising mechanisms that may account for at least some of these unusual signals, although important questions remain unanswered.

For now, long-delayed echoes serve as a reminder of the challenges of studying electromagnetic phenomena, and how even seemingly familiar aspects of our physical world can harbor mysteries that resist straightforward explanations, even after nearly a century of investigation.

A new stack of Starlink satellites is now in orbit following an early morning SpaceX launch from California.

Falcon 9's upper stage ignited its engine for a second time about 53 minutes after liftoff, circularizing its orbit with a burn that lasted a very short 3 seconds. That was followed several minutes later by the deployment of the rocket's Starlink payloads.

SpaceX's Starlink network consists of more than 11,000 active spacecraft. The speed with which the company is delivering them to orbit in bulk, however, has slowed somewhat.

As SpaceX shifts focus to its larger, more powerful Starship rocket under development, plans to retire Falcon 9 have already begun. Part of that process included ending Starlink launches from Florida earlier this year.

B1082 successfullly landed on OCISLY at T+8:23, seconds before Falcon 9's second stage completed its first engine burn. The return of B1082 marks the booster's 21st Starlink mission, and 26th overall flight, the others of which include USSF-62, OneWeb Launch 20, NROL-145, Transporter-18.

Falcon 9's upper stage ignited its engine for a second time about 53 minutes after liftoff, circularizing its orbit with a burn that lasted a very short 3 seconds. That was followed several minutes later by the deployment of the rocket's Starlink payloads.

Previous Booster B1082 launches

USSF-62 | OneWeb Launch 20 | NROL-145 | Transporter-18 | 26 Starlink missions

SpaceX's Starlink network consists of more than 11,000 active spacecraft. The speed with which the company is delivering them to orbit in bulk, however, has slowed somewhat.

As SpaceX shifts focus to its larger, more powerful Starship rocket under development, plans to retire Falcon 9 have already begun. Part of that process included ending Starlink launches from Florida earlier this year.

Today's mission was the 117th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, so far. About three-quarters of those were dedicated to Starlink.

 <description>Irácký soud v úterý uložil doživotní tresty šesti francouzským občanům, které shledal vinnými z příslušnosti k takzvanému Islámskému státu (IS). Spolu s ním se ke stejnému kroku rozhodli i další nově zvolení zastupitelé Semil na kandidátce ANO Semily. Nově budou fungovat jako nezávislí.</description></item><item><title>Jak budou mít obchody otevřeno 28. října? Přehled před svátečním nákupem</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904167-jak-budou-mit-obchody-otevreno-28-rijna-prehled-pred-svatecnim-nakupem.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904167-jak-budou-mit-obchody-otevreno-28-rijna-prehled-pred-svatecnim-nakupem.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 20:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Markéta Hamerníková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Na větší nákup bude potřeba vyrazit předem. Ve středu 28. října musí většina obchodů s prodejní plochou nad 200 metrů čtverečních zavřít. Menší prodejny mohou otevřít, výjimku mají také čerpací stanice, lékárny nebo vybrané obchody na nádražích.</description></item><item><title>Slovan postupuje do čtvrtfinále poháru. Teplice udolal 1:0</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/904253-slovan-postupuje-do-ctvrtfinale-poharu-teplice-udolal-1-0.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/904253-slovan-postupuje-do-ctvrtfinale-poharu-teplice-udolal-1-0.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 19:04:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Liberečtí fotbalisté si zahrají čtvrtfinále domácího poháru. Proti neoblíbeným Teplicím stačila jediná branka, kterou už v první půli vstřelil Mašek.</description></item><item><title>Veterináři zrušili poslední pásmo vymezené v ČR kvůli africkému moru prasat</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/904213-veterinari-zrusili-posledni-pasmo-vymezene-v-cr-kvuli-africkemu-moru-prasat.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/904213-veterinari-zrusili-posledni-pasmo-vymezene-v-cr-kvuli-africkemu-moru-prasat.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 18:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Veterináři zrušili poslední pásmo vymezené kvůli africkému moru prasat v Libereckém kraji. Zrušením pásma přestávají platit opatření, která dopadala zejména na místní chovatele a myslivce. Chovatelé prasat domácích tak už nebudou muset být dvakrát ročně úředně kontrolováni.</description></item><item><title>Halloween pochází z Irska. Jak se z keltské tradice stal svátek, který slaví celý svět</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904102-halloween-pochazi-z-irska-jak-se-z-keltske-tradice-stal-svatek-ktery-slavi-cely-svet.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904102-halloween-pochazi-z-irska-jak-se-z-keltske-tradice-stal-svatek-ktery-slavi-cely-svet.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 16:54:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Masky, strašidelné kostýmy, vydlabané dýně, oheň a večírky. Halloween dnes zná téměř celý svět. Jeho kořeny bychom ale hledali v Irsku, kde se před více než tisíci lety slavila keltská tradice Samhain. Právě ta položila základy svátku, který dnes patří k nejvýraznějším oslavám podzimu.</description></item><item><title>Když si na to ukážu, tak to seberu. Zloděj v Lípě hájil krádež kola</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904171-kdyz-si-na-to-ukazu-tak-to-seberu-zlodej-v-lipe-hajil-kradez-kola.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904171-kdyz-si-na-to-ukazu-tak-to-seberu-zlodej-v-lipe-hajil-kradez-kola.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:03:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Krátce po půlnoci byla strážníkům v České Lípě nahlášena krádež kola. Hlídka ale zloděje vypátrala vlastně za pár minut. Muž, který kolo vzal, se pak strážníkům originálně vymlouval, přesto ho čeká správní řízení.</description></item><item><title>Mimořádný triumf: Jablonecký sbor Iuventus, gaude! získal ve Španělsku dvě zlata</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904159-mimoradny-triumf-jablonecky-sbor-iuventus-gaude-ziskal-ve-spanelsku-dve-zlata.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904159-mimoradny-triumf-jablonecky-sbor-iuventus-gaude-ziskal-ve-spanelsku-dve-zlata.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 14:10:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Dětský pěvecký sbor Iuventus, gaude! ze ZUŠ Jablonec nad Nisou zaznamenal obrovský světový úspěch. Na prestižní soutěži SING FOR GOLD 2026 ve španělské Calelle vybojoval v konkurenci 35 těles ze 22 zemí dvě zlatá pásma a zajistil si přímou kvalifikaci na mezinárodní vrcholné akce na dalších 5 let.</description></item><item><title>Osm kilo stříbra a drahokamy: V Turnově vystaví unikátní relikviář sv. Václava</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/904151-osm-kilo-stribra-a-drahokamy-v-turnove-vystavi-unikatni-relikviar-sv-vaclava.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/904151-osm-kilo-stribra-a-drahokamy-v-turnove-vystavi-unikatni-relikviar-sv-vaclava.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Kultura</category><description>V Muzeu Českého ráje v Turnově bude od 29. října do 29. listopadu 2026 k vidění nový relikviář svatého Václava. Výjimečný klenot z osmikilogramového stříbra a drahých kamenů vytvořil turnovský zlatník Jiří Urban s týmem dalších odborníků.</description></item><item><title>Oprava silnice I/35 zkomplikuje od středy dopravu na výjezdu z Turnova na Jičín</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/904144-oprava-silnice-i-35-zkomplikuje-od-stredy-dopravu-na-vyjezdu-z-turnova-na.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/904144-oprava-silnice-i-35-zkomplikuje-od-stredy-dopravu-na-vyjezdu-z-turnova-na.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Oprava povrchu na zhruba půlkilometrovém úseku silnice I/35 zkomplikuje od středy dopravu na výjezdu z Turnova na Semilsku směrem na Jičín. Doprava bude svedena na polovinu vozovky a řízena kyvadlově. Práce by měly skončit v sobotu dopoledne.</description></item><item><title>Rekonstrukce libereckého bazénu aktuálně: Otevření pro veřejnost v září 2027 platí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904157-rekonstrukce-libereckeho-bazenu-aktualne-otevreni-pro-verejnost-v-zari-2027-plati.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904157-rekonstrukce-libereckeho-bazenu-aktualne-otevreni-pro-verejnost-v-zari-2027-plati.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 27 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Rozsáhlá kompletní obnova libereckého plaveckého stadionu, která začala v listopadu 2024, úspěšně pokračuje. Pravidelná a tradiční sportovní soutěž škol Šluknovského výběžku (dle loňských textů letos 34. ročník). A jako vždy dílčí informace od některých účastnících se škol:

Základní škola Jiříkov:

Ve středu 21. 10. 2026 byl futsalovým turnajem zahájen další ročník Šluknovské ligy. V Dolní Poustevně jsme byli první !!!. Až později dorazil do haly domácí tým a po něm zbývající 4 družstva. Tím náš velký úspěch skončil. Naši hráči se snažili trefit správné zařízení, kterému se říká branka soupeře, a nakonec se nám tato činnost dolní končetiny povedla 4x a pokaždé jinému střelci. Šancí bylo více, ale na ty se nehraje. Trochu jsme zamotali tabulkou svým jediným vítězstvím nad třetím Šluknovem, ale nakonec jsme se umístili na 6. místě. Nutno podotknout, že polovinu našeho repre týmu tvořili nováčci ze 6. třídy, pro které byla velká zkušenost hrát proti o dva až tři roky starším chlapcům. Nejdůležitější je, že si všichni zahráli, naši kluci zůstali zdraví, nikdo nebyl CHORÝ a chovali se v rámci fair-play. Za měsíc jdou do boje děvčata v přehazované, tak jim držme palce, aby naše umístění vylepšila.

J. Kolář

Šluknovská liga – futsal. ZŠ Dolní Poustevna – krásné 4. místo. Gratulujeme!

První sportovní soutěží Šluknovské ligy v ročníku 2026/2027 byl, jako již tradičně, futsal.

Náš tým tvořili žáci napříč celým druhým stupněm: Kristián D., Antonín V., Matyáš H., Matyáš H., Josef B., Jakub V., G. C., David V. a Petr S.

Všem hráčům děkujeme za jejich nasazení, sportovní přístup a reprezentaci školy.

]]> Turnaj Jr. NBA League, 1. hrací kolo divize E – 21. 10. 2026 Šluknov https://www.vybezek.eu/296193-turnaj-jr-nba-league-1-hraci-kolo-divize-e-21-10-2026-sluknov/ Wed, 21 Oct 2026 21:49:30 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296193 Po jarní kvalifikační části (a po divizi F ve VDF) se ve středu 21. října 2026 konal turnaj dalšího ročníku Jr. NBA League ve Šluknově.

Web Schrödingerova institutu:

Ve středu 21. října se ve Šluknově odehrálo hrací kolo Západní ligy Jr. NBA, divize E, které organizačně zajistila Basketbalová akademie Šluknovska při Schrödingerově institutu.

Na palubovce se představilo pět školních týmů, které bojovaly nejen o vítězství, ale především o dvě postupová místa do další fáze soutěže.

Konečné pořadí divize E:
1. ZŠ Mozartova, Jablonec nad Nisou
2. ZŠ Vojtěcha Kováře, Rumburk
3. ZŠ Tyršova, Rumburk
4. ZŠ J. Vohradského, Šluknov
5. ZŠ Jiříkov

O druhém postupujícím rozhodoval doslova jediný bod! Obě rumburské školy odehrály vzájemný zápas s nerozhodným výsledkem 6:6 a o konečném pořadí tak rozhodoval rozdíl ve skóre ze všech utkání. Ten měla ZŠ Vojtěcha Kováře lepší o pouhý jeden bod, a zajistila si tak postup společně s vítěznou školou z Jablonce nad Nisou. Šluknovská základní škola obsadila se svým jedním vítězstvím čtvrté místo, pátý Jiříkov tentokrát na výhru nedosáhl.

Gratulujeme oběma postupujícím týmům a všem ostatním děkujeme za skvělé sportovní nasazení, bojovnost a fair play! Velké poděkování patří také všem, kteří se podíleli na organizaci turnaje, trenérům, pedagogům i rozhodčím.

Jsme rádi, že Basketbalová akademie Šluknovska může být součástí projektu Jr. NBA a přinášet dětem z našeho regionu další příležitosti zažít atmosféru opravdové basketbalové soutěže.
Basketbal nás spojuje!

Oficiální web akce je na tom stále stejně (viz minulý text), nic nic nic a ještě jednou nic. A tentokrát na tom o moc lépe nejsou ani zúčastněné školy.

Základní škola Jiříkov na FB:

Žáci ZŠ Jiříkov bojovali v juniorské NBA lize

Dne 21. 10. 2026 se žáci 2. až 5. tříd ZŠ Jiříkov zúčastnili juniorské NBA ligy, kde bojovali o postup do dalšího kola.

Přestože se jim tentokrát nepodařilo zvítězit a postoupit do užšího výběru, zaslouží si velkou pochvalu. Do hry dali všechny své síly, bojovali statečně a nevzdávali se. Ukázali své přednosti a zároveň poznali, v čem se mohou dál zlepšovat.

Zápasy jim přinesly cenné zkušenosti i motivaci do dalších tréninků. Děkujeme všem našim hráčům a hráčkám za reprezentaci školy, nasazení a odhodlání!

Přijďte strávit příjemné odpoledne na Asijskou poznávací stezku, kde společně oslavíme Slavnost světel a pro letošek stezku symbolicky zavřeme.

Rodiny s dětmi se od 15:30 mohou těšit na tvořivé dílny a kouzelnou procházku s lampiony osvětlenou stezkou. Nenechte si ujít vznik nádherného vzoru rangoli z barevného písku inspirovaného indickým svátkem světel – Díválí. Na zahřátí si můžete vychutnat šálek kořeněného masala čaje.

Dospělí návštěvníci se mohou zapojit do rozebírání jurty před zimou, vlhké zimní klima jí nesvědčí…

Přijďte s lampionem a můžete vzít i menší zavařovací sklenici na ozdobení, kterou si odnesete i se světýlkem.

Věříme, že společně strávíme příjemný podvečer. Těšíme se na vás!
